NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
MECHANISM CLASS: Feed-to-Quench Duty Split
The proposed intervention is a re-tuning of the quench-schedule procedure and feed-ratio setpoint to maintain the catalyst bed at a lower effective reaction temperature, thereby shifting the equilibrium limit upward. Standard practice relies on fixed quench gas flows that assume a steady-state exotherm; this mitigation dynamically increases quench flow proportionally to instantaneous exotherm to counteract the temperature rise that drives the equilibrium trap. The adjacent-technique clearance is the use of feed-forward control on quench lines in multi-bed synthesis; the departure is the explicit coupling of quench duty to the *declining conversion* indicator (per-pass conversion) to actively cool the bed as activity wanes, rather than maintaining a fixed temperature setpoint. The mechanism attacks the driving physics by lowering the local bed temperature, which increases the equilibrium conversion constant for the exothermic hydrogenation reaction.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing relation: $K_{eq}(T) = \exp(-\Delta H^\circ / RT + \Delta S^\circ / R)$. For exothermic hydrogenation ($\Delta H < 0$), $K_{eq}$ decreases as temperature $T$ increases.
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = Bed Temperature ($T_{bed}$); the mechanism moves it DOWN by ~10-15°C through increased quench gas dilution/cooling; this REDUCES the equilibrium limitation ($X_{eq}$ increases), thereby restoring the per-pass conversion margin.
Magnitude verification: At 230°C, a 10°C drop increases $K_{eq}$ by a factor of approximately $\exp(\Delta H/R \cdot (1/T_2 - 1/T_1))$. With $\Delta H \approx -90$ kJ/mol, the shift is significant enough to counteract the ~5-10% conversion loss typical of mild catalyst aging or off-design feed.
INPUT-AVAILABILITY CLAUSE: The remedy requires online signals for: (1) Bed Temperature (existing thermocouples), (2) Per-pass Conversion (derived from existing online analyzer flow rates/compositions or estimated from product stream pressure drop and flow data stated in infrastructure). Both are derivable from stated existing instruments.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
(a) Existing Control Valve on Quench Gas Line, re-tuned.
(b) Existing DCS/PLC Program for Quench Schedule, modified to link quench flow setpoint to a lower-bed-temperature target (e.g., 220°C) instead of fixed flow.
(c) Existing Feed-Gas Ratio Setpoint, adjusted to 1:1.5 H2:CO2 (from standard 1:2) to reduce exotherm rate per unit of conversion, allowing lower temperature operation for same production rate.
(c) Operational Procedure: Operator adjusts quench gas flow manually every 2 hours to hold the downstream bed inlet temperature at 215°C (a 15°C drop from nominal 230°C), using the existing control valve.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
(a) Control Valve re-tuning: Cost = 0 (labor only); Burden = Low (standard procedure).
(b) DCS Program Change: Cost = 0 (software change); Burden = Low (standard commissioning task).
(c) Feed-Ratio Change: Cost = 0; Burden = Negligible (operational parameter change).
Operational Loss Pricing: Lower temperature operation reduces reaction rate, necessitating a 5% lower total feed flow to maintain conversion margin. This results in a 5% throughput reduction. Trade-off: Throughput loss (-5%) is offset by prevention of off-spec gas recirculation energy costs and catalyst damage from hot spots, netting positive over 6-month horizon.
EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Run converter at standard feed ratio for 48h (baseline). Switch to proposed feed ratio (1:1.5 H2:CO2) and manual quench schedule (holding bed inlet at 215°C) for 48h.
Instruments: Existing bed thermocouples, existing online gas analyzer, DCS historian.
Pass/Fail Threshold: Per-pass CO2 conversion measured by analyzer must increase by $\ge$ 3% relative to baseline, OR bed temperature variance must decrease by $\ge$ 20% without conversion drop.
Duration: 96 hours total.
Kill Criterion: If conversion drops by >2% or bed temperature exceeds 240°C during the test period, abort and revert to standard settings.
